An opening is delivered anyway, not withheld pending the number

analyst_notes: The pass rate understates the skill, and the reason matters more than the number. Three of the four with-skill runs dispatched oratores-critic on their own draft and acted on its findings BEFORE writing the file the grader reads. So the assertions measure the post-review output, and the mechanism that produced the difference is invisible in the score.

What the critic caught inside those runs, self-reported by each: 13 confirmed findings on the pitch opening including two of that run's own regressions; 18 confirmed defects on the reorg structure, the worst being four claim-ledger rows marked CHECKED against a plan the agent was never given; and on the conference close, two invented quantities ('twice the on-call', 'a quarter') in a piece whose own notes claimed none.

Two runs independently reached the same conclusion in their own words. One: 'a self-audit sitting next to the text suppresses the check - my notes claimed no invented numbers (there were two), one coined line (four), 176 words (227). Every error failed in the passing direction.' The other: 'All fail in the passing direction: the deliverable looks audited by the thing it names.' Neither saw the other.

eval-0 does not discriminate and is kept as a guard, not a win condition. The baseline handles a one-minute toast well unaided (129 spoken words vs 124). What it verifies is that the skill does not inflate a small task - and the skill loaded zero modules for it, which is the proportional-execution claim holding.

The cost is real and should not be buried: roughly 5x the tokens and 7x the wall time. On a one-minute toast that is a bad trade. On a piece with numbers in it, the invented quantities the critic stripped are the trade.

FOUR OF TWELVE ASSERTIONS WERE WRONG, all against the skill, and each needed a separate fix: summing every blockquote counted an alternate 30-second cut as part of the main toast (189 reported for 131); a 600-word cap penalised the skill for offering priced alternates, which is the feature; a 'you will' bigram flagged 'the way you will say it' as a claim of authority; and the no-invented-figure check flagged a properly cited BMC Health Serv Res study with a DOI, and a figure quoted expressly to warn against using it. The instrumentation was wrong more often than the skill was.

Reproducibility check: the first benchmark was assembled from grading.json files written by an earlier run of the grader, before its last correction, and reported 30/32 where the published grader gives 29/32. The numbers here are re-derived from a single run of the grader that ships in evals/. A published number that disagrees with the published tool is the same defect this package spent the day removing.

HEADLINE CORRECTION: the delta is +0.05, not the +0.113 first reported. The first figure came from a stale benchmark assembled before the grader's last fix. With the one unreliable assertion excluded, with_skill is 15/15 and without_skill 14/15 on the checks that hold - a one-assertion gap across four tasks. On these single well-posed prompts the skill's measurable advantage is small and the cost is 5x tokens and 7x wall time.

unreliable_assertions.assertion: Every figure about no-show losses either carries a locator or is explicitly disowned
unreliable_assertions.why: Rewritten three times and still failing the with_skill run, whose behaviour is manifestly correct: it fetched a page to check the $150bn provenance, found a 2024 trade release from a medical-transportation company crediting no source, recorded status UNVERIFIED with the reason, kept the figure out of the script, cited Kheirkhah et al. 2016 BMC Health Serv Res 16:13 with a DOI and a verbatim sentence, and refused to splice the FY2008 dollar figure onto a twelve-year mean rate. The disowning language is spread across paragraphs in notes.md that no fixed-width neighbourhood window captures. An assertion that needs a fourth adjustment before it agrees with the grader is not measuring the thing; it is measuring the grader.
